Acting CJ Antonio T. Carpio: longest-serving current SC member; chairman of the Court's Second Division; 'foremost advocate of our sovereign rights in the West Philippine Sea'; patient and distinguished chairman of the Board of Judges for 2017-2018 FLP Law Scholarship Contest; interviewed applicants at SC Division Conference Rooms ('the sacred inner sanctum of the temple of justice... only the justices are allowed entry when they deliberate and decide Division cases -- no secretaries, clerks or aides dare enter')

Velasco Jr.: second longest-serving SC member; chairman of Third Division; chairman of Board of Judges for Dissertation Writing Contest; both Carpio and Velasco 'were my contemporaries and were already serving the highest court of the land when I was the incumbent Chief Justice'

Other judges: former Education Secretary Edilberto C. de Jesus (AIM president and retired professor; FEU president; wife Leni taught with him for 37 years); Dean Sedfrey M. 21 scholars from all over the country: University of the Cordilleras (Northern Luzon), major Metro Manila law schools, USC and U Cebu (Visayas), St. Thomas More College (Mindanao)

Dissertation winners: Rafael Lorenzo Pangalangan (Oxford/UP; 1st, P300,000 + gold plaque); Tess Marie Tan (USC; 2nd, also FLP scholar last year); four finalists: Rexlyn Anne Evora (PUP), Helen May Frias (FEU), Janine Faye Napoles (Centro Escolar), Joben Mariz Odulio (Ateneo)

stances.claim: The privilege of being interviewed in the SC's Division Conference Rooms -- where 'only the justices are allowed entry when they deliberate and decide Division cases' -- is itself a form of recognition before these scholars even pass the bar exam. The sacred-inner-sanctum framing is a design choice by Acting CJ Carpio and Justice Velasco that confers institutional prestige on FLP's scholars.
stances.rhetorical_move: sacred-inner-sanctum argument: the interview venue is a deliberate honor that pre-validates the scholars' status

stances.claim: The two-drivers-and-bosses joke, delivered as the icebreaker, is a due-process parable: before condemning the drivers (or anyone), hear them first; both sides have reasonable perspectives. The joke implicitly endorses procedural fairness as a governing value for the legal profession.
stances.rhetorical_move: due-process parable embedded in a joke: comedy as a vehicle for legal principle
stances.confidence: asserted with explicit framing ('let us accord due process to the drivers')

stances.claim: Tess Marie Tan's dissertation on Internet intermediaries -- written months before the Senate hearing raised the same topic -- demonstrates that the FLP Dissertation Contest produces original scholarship that anticipates real policy debates. FLP will feature it in CJP's Inquirer column as proof of relevance.
stances.rhetorical_move: timeliness-as-relevance proof: the dissertation's anticipation of the Senate hearing as the strongest evidence of FLP's practical value
stances.confidence: asserted as an immediate, contemporaneous example

notable_anecdotes: The two-drivers-and-bosses joke: two lawyers complain about their stupid drivers. First driver's response: 'He has a cell phone. He should just have called his office.' Second driver's response: 'If he is not so stupid, he should have specified the color of the car he wanted.' The lawyers were the stupid ones. Due process: hear all sides before judging.

Acting CJ Carpio's Division Conference Room interviews: 'These rooms constitute the sacred inner sanctum of the temple of justice in our country where only the justices are allowed entry when they deliberate and decide Division cases. No secretaries, clerks or aides dare enter these rooms when the justices perform their rituals and duties.' -- opened for FLP scholarship interviews.

Tess Marie Tan's timeliness: her dissertation on Internet intermediary liability was written before the Senate Committee hearing chaired by Sen. Grace Poe where Facebook liability was raised. CJP will feature it in his Inquirer column March 25, 2018.
Rafael Pangalangan's credentials: from Oxford University and the University of the Philippines -- 1st place, P300,000 + gold plaque.

one_paragraph_summary: Delivered March 23, 2018 at the FLP Awards Ceremony at Ateneo de Manila Professional Schools, this closing address by CJP opens with the two-drivers-and-bosses joke -- where both lawyers' drivers turn out to be the rational ones after due-process treatment ('he has a cell phone; he should just have called'; 'he should have specified the color of the car he wanted') -- as a parable for procedural fairness. He thanks Acting CJ Antonio T. Carpio ('foremost advocate of our sovereign rights in the West Philippine Sea'; longest-serving SC member; chaired the Scholarship Board of Judges, opening the SC Division Conference Rooms -- 'the sacred inner sanctum of the temple of justice... where only the justices are allowed entry') and Justice Presbitero J. Velasco Jr. (second longest-serving; chaired the Dissertation Board of Judges). Other judges: Dr. Edilberto de Jesus (AIM/FEU/former Edu Sec; wife Leni taught with him 37 years at AIM), Dean Sedfrey Candelaria (Ateneo; PALS president; FLP chair holder), Ms. Elizabeth Alba (TYK Foundation), and Joel Emerson Gregorio (ADB; FLP trustee). He thanks the Tan Yan Kee Foundation and Ayala Corporation (Jaime Zobel 'immediately and unhesitatingly agreed' to fund the Dissertation Contest as an extra to Ayala's philanthropy budget). He hails the 21 scholars from across the country (Cordilleras, Metro Manila, USC, U Cebu, St. Thomas More) and the dissertation winners: Rafael Pangalangan of Oxford/UP (1st, P300,000), Tess Marie Tan of USC (2nd, also former FLP scholar; her work on Internet intermediaries was published weeks before the same issue arose in a Senate hearing chaired by Sen. Grace Poe -- to be featured in CJP's March 25 Inquirer column), and four finalists (Evora/PUP, Frias/FEU, Napoles/Centro Escolar, Odulio/Ateneo). He announces new exclusive cash awards for Latin honors graduates and future bar topnotchers, and reaffirms the merit-first-need-as-tiebreaker selection principle.
